modelOverview: The RM 43-01 Tourbillon Split-Seconds Chronograph Ferrari is the second watch from Richard Mille's partnership with Ferrari, unveiled in Paris in 2025 after three years of development. Built with Audemars Piguet Le Locle, its 514-component manual-winding calibre pairs a tourbillon with a split-seconds chronograph and is produced in 150 pieces split between Carbon TPT and microblasted titanium.

RM 43-01.movement: Manual · Richard Mille Calibre RM43-01 · tourbillon · split-seconds chronograph · 30-minute totaliser · power-reserve, torque and function indicators · 21,600vph · ~70h power reserve
RM 43-01.materials: Limited edition of 75 pieces in Carbon TPT and 75 pieces in microblasted grade 5 titanium with a Carbon TPT caseband
RM 43-01.dial: Skeletonised grade 5 titanium baseplate with tourbillon at 5 o'clock, 30-minute counter at 9 o'clock, five-blade rotating seconds display, power-reserve and torque indicators and a W/N/H function window; beige and red accents on titanium, grey and yellow on Carbon TPT
RM 43-01.description: The RM 43-01 Tourbillon Split-Seconds Chronograph Ferrari returns the partnership to Richard Mille's tonneau case, housing a 514-part manual-winding movement that combines a tourbillon with a rattrapante chronograph, torque and power-reserve indicators and a seconds display of five rotating blades. It is made in 75 pieces in Carbon TPT and 75 in microblasted titanium, each with its own accent colours. Every piece we offer is sourced and independently authenticated before sale.
